newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain fulfils inflation criteria with Feb CPI.
newsitem.headline: Spain fulfils inflation criteria with Feb CPI.

text.p: MADRID, March 13 (REuter) - After a sharp drop in February inflation, Spain now fulfils the criteria for inflation for Europe's single currency, the Economy Ministry said.
"February CPI puts Spain within convergence limits on inflation," the Ministry said in a statement.
Spanish inflation fell to a 2.5 percent year-on-year rate in February from 2.9 percent in January.
According to the convergence rules, a country's inflation rate may not exceed the average of the three best performers by more than 1.5 percentage points.
"The year-on-year inflation rate has experienced a new and significant decline of four-tenths in the month of February, falling to 2.5 percent," the statement said.
"Therefore, there has been an accumulated fall of seven-tenths in just two months and the government reaches its inflation target for the end of the year at 2.6 percent."
Analysts had expected moderation to 2.7 or 2.8 percent, and said all areas had performed well except service prices.
Services, with a year-on-year rate of 3.6 percent "continue stuck at the same level as the last nine months," the statement said.
But the ministry said it expected improvement as new wage packages show moderation.
